_doc: T-269 (docs/u21/t269_zombie_look.md): what the walkers wear and how dead they look, per map. Nothing here adds a mesh, a material or a texture: an outfit is three colours (a = the kit's main cloth, b = its second cloth, c = the accent: scarf, shawl, cap, oilskin, hood) written to per-instance shader parameters of the two shared zombie materials, a skin is a tone and a mottling amount. Colours are sRGB hex as they should read in a neutral light; the map's grade then takes about half of the saturation away (data/look/<map>.json mono), which is why they are stronger here than the art bible's 30 % box. pattern: none | stripes | check | dots (on colour a; pattern_color optional, else a darker a). maps.<map>.<kit>: outfit -> weight; a kit a map does not list takes maps.default.<kit>; a kit listed nowhere keeps its baked colours (the Soviet risen, the drowned, the Bellringer). Only plain Gangers are dressed: specials and bosses keep their own look so they stand apart. The choice is a hash of the zombie's net id and its spawn health (ZombieWardrobe.look_seed): the same on host and clients, nothing is sent.

slots._doc: Which part key of a kit's clothes takes which colour (1 = a, 2 = b, 3 = c; a key not listed keeps its own). kit_slots overrides per kit. Gear pieces use the shared table only.

light._doc: Readability in the dark, in the zombie materials only (no map light changes): min_light = the share of its own colour a zombie shows with no light on it at all; rim = a soft edge light tinted by the cloth / skin under it (rim_power: how tight to the silhouette). `-- --zombie-look=norim` switches both off for an A/B.

wear._doc: On top of the colour: blood = the range of the per-zombie stain amount on clothes, mouth and hands (0..1); stain_color the dried blood; dead = the range of how sunken the sockets, mouth and hands are and how dark the veins under the skin; frost_scale = how much of the map's standing rime (anim.json variation.frost_by_map, tuned on the old pale cloth) a dressed walker keeps: on a colour the full amount reads as white mould. A weapon's freeze is not scaled.

skins._doc: tone multiplies the kit's skin colour, mottle (0..1) is how much of the bruise colour shows in blotches.

maps._doc: Per map and kit: outfit -> weight.

map00_crossroads._doc: The inn and the village: farmhands, the inn's own people, a postman, the priest, a railwayman, a hunter, Sunday clothes, people caught in their nightshirts; soldiers of the occupation force in field green; the odd miner come down from Kaltenbrunn.

map01_kaltenbrunn._doc: The mine town: ochre and rust overalls, blue drill, the overseers in shirt and waistcoat; the Werk's lab staff and technicians.

map02_totenhafen._doc: The harbour: dockers and fishermen in wool, sailors in navy, stripes and oilskins.

map04a_thalbach._doc: Werk Thalbach: factory hands in coveralls, townspeople, the guard.

map04b_kranich._doc: The flight: ground crew in coveralls, flight crew in leather and blue with a pale scarf.

map04c_groomlake._doc: The test site: lab coats, coveralls bleached by the desert.

map04d_mondlicht._doc: The Moon: pressure suits. The map's grade is black and white by rule (violet the only colour), so these differ in value, not hue: pale, tan and dark suits.
